notes.title: Tempest Tower is Out Now!!
notes.content:
Today is the day, Tempest Tower has officially released into Steam Early Access! Tempest Tower is an action-packed Tower Defense game with Platforming elements. You must explore, plan, and meticulously construct your base during the Build Phase. Then, execute, adapt, and ruthlessly brawl with hordes of Creepers during the Action Phase.

If that sounds like it might be for you, then check out Tempest Tower on Steam right now. If you're still on the fence then we have a demo available that you can try before you buy.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3123800/Tempest_Tower/

[h2]Introducing the HPY bundle![/h2]
Tempest Tower is Half Past Yellow's second commercial game (if you want to see some of our less commercial titles you can take a look at [url=https://halfpastyellow.itch.io/]our itch page[/url]). To celebrate this we have created a Tempest Tower x Time on Frog Island bundle, so if you have been on the fence about buying ToFI after trying the prologue, then there has never been a better time to get on board! [url=https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/50600/]Check it out here[/url].

notes.title: Take a look at Tempest Tower
notes.content:
Hello Sailors!

notes.title: Time on Frog Island | Meet The Blacksmith
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Meet [b]The Blacksmith![/b]

The Blacksmith is one of two frogs on the island who build and maintain the infrastructure around the island. Alongside The Carpenter, The Blacksmith is well respected and held in high regard on the island. 

Concept Art
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/18dc83025e5622636c9f40865a15e01f55f2dd16.png[/img]

Her heavy breathing keeps the fires of her forge burning while she works and no one would want to be in front of her when she yells. The Blacksmith likes to only work on one project at a time, she thinks it is too hard to keep things separate in her head. If you need something done, you will have to wait in line with your order like everyone else.

The Blacksmith was wary of The Sailor on the day he arrived, she was finishing up a project and refused to even look at or talk to the strange creature. That evening was when her tadpup went missing, meaning The Blacksmith had bigger things to worry about than an island visitor...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/2ef75031873db8ccd62bc2f4ea0ad946e2a3ba72.gif[/img]

notes.title: Meet the Farmer
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Meet Frog Islands resident farmer!

The Farmer is easily flustered and can’t think straight when things aren’t going according to plan. She spends her time caring for a small farm on the outskirts of town, exclusively growing fruits because she is allergic to any and all wildlife.

The Farmer has a small fruit stall by her house with an honesty box for other frogs to drop trades into, but most frogs around the island take advantage of this generosity. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/8ebb86e5832d27e67e85a2f3e2c62fa75704f30d.png[/img]

The Farmer is a total neat freak and keeps her different crops segmented with fences to avoid horticultural fraternisation.

The Farmer is preoccupied when The Sailor first arrives on the island and has no time to stop and stare. Under normal circumstances, she may have been more surprised/uncomfortable/shy, but there is no time for any of that while her crop is being decimated by pesky crows...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/49308b4b0fe10602601f543e338a22b30a412ea4.png[/img]

We've got more froggy friends from Frog Island to share to stay tuned for the next update!

notes.title: Time on Frog Island!
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

We're very excited to share with you that Trading Time: A Croak Tale has been given a fresh new name! Trading Time is now [b]Time on Frog Island[/b]!

Why the name change? When we were localising the name for our Chinese players, the name we went with translated in English to Time on Frog Island, as our original title didn't quite make sense directly translated into Chinese.

We all really liked Time on Frog Island, and some seeds were sown! As time went on and players resonated more and more with the cast of froggy characters in the game, we decided that we really wanted to reflect the froggy nature of the game more in the title, so here we are!

notes.title: Meet the residents of Croak Island
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

We're very excited to start revealing more about the totally-normal native islander society of our game! Yeah no, "normal" probably isn't the right word... Regardless, as it so happens, the island that our Sailor has shipwrecked on is inhabited by a small town of large humanoid frogs! 🧍🐸! Let's start with introducing The Carpenter!

The Carpenter is tasked with creating and maintaining all the wooden structures on the island. Being the only real handyfrog available, he is always busy. Unfortunately, he is also constantly falling behind on his tasks by always misplacing the exact tool needed for the job. He could definitely use a helping hand to find them so you better keep an eye out as you explore the island!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/18da3bfedd64f509675d30e38a618ca3e865fa6c.png[/img]

Why frogs, you ask? Well, we needed some island natives and asked ourselves, "What if humans stemmed from frogs instead of apes and were left alone on an island all to themselves?" Naturally, this is it. You're looking at the first character of many in the only possible outcome of our highly scientific research and plentiful discussions on the matter.

[h1]Early Concept Art[/h1]
The Carpenter can be considered one of the simpler characters in our cast of villagers and we wanted his visual design to reflect that. Dressed in a plain vest and undersized beanie, his glassy-eyed expression almost never changes no matter the circumstance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/12229308069c301614fdcb85e578f2db70699391.png[/img]

[h1]Have you seen my tool?[/h1]
Don't let his blank gaze fool you, however! He's a master craftsman that can build almost anything and will certainly prove it to you! Just.. ah...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/34a852ca929d11daf273849d6414210be02b3081.gif[/img]

Well... He's gone and lost his tool again! Maybe we can help him find it? Oh! Is that it?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/a010bb092103661c8ec46937e8cd895b68309c7b.gif[/img]

It's a saw! Of course, it is! Obviously, you can't be a carpenter without it. Good job, everyone! Clearly, the nature of a blog means that this is almost as far from the actual gameplay as is possible but the sense of accomplishment and helpfulness is almost just as real. Trust me, though, when I say it won't always be quite so easy to find what you need strewn about the island...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/22b7948256950aac8f59081555757b0b5d58bb7f.gif[/img]

Now that he's got his saw back he can get to work! Let's leave him to it and check back later. Maybe some other townsfolk could use some help in the meantime? 

Say tuned to meet more of the Croak Island locals in future updates!

notes.title: Controlling the Sun
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Up until now, you've seen bright and sunny images of our island but what if we told you there was another side to it? Let there be... Night!

A core feature of our game is a day/night cycle that has different gameplay opportunities depending on the time of day. Not only was it important to us to have each time of day to look and feel distinct from the others, but they needed to also transition nicely from one to the next. Oh, and also you need to be able to see what you're doing when it's dark.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/jQyIrlc.gif[/img]

During normal gameplay each distinct time of day in the game lasts several minutes - so don't worry, there's plenty of time to explore and get things done while it's still light out!

What we're essentially doing is defining specific times of day and setting it up for the look we want. Then during gameplay, we interpolate between the current phase's settings and the next one based on the time in-game. We have split the day into six phases: Morning, Noon, Afternoon, Dusk, Night, and Late Night. In our case, Late Night is indefinite and doesn't need to transition into Morning otherwise it would probably make sense to also have a Dawn phase.

The settings we are defining to provide the biggest visual impact between the phases are:

[b]The Sun Light[/b]
[list]
[*] Color
[*] Direction
[/list]
[b]Fog[/b]
[list]
[*] Color
[*] Density
[/list]
[b]Post Processing[/b]
[list]
[*] Color Correction
[*] Vignette
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/49c1e259227a15f8e27770582a031560e3b0166e.png[/img]

As you can see, some settings change quite significantly from one phase to the next but it doesn't feel quite so drastic in-game since the gradual interpolation handles it all for us very nicely. Nighttime clearly stands out over the rest, and that's certainly intentional seeing as most of the time players will be out during the day and taking nightfall as a signal to rest and prepare for the next day.

That's all, folks! It's a bit of a short post this time around since there's not much more to say and the images pretty much speak for themselves. It's probably worth mentioning that configuring every setting for each phase can be very time consuming and we've spent many hours (and will probably continue spending many more!) making small adjustments here and there to ensure that everything looks right no matter the time.

As always, if you have any specific questions or comments about any of this, just pop on in to our Discord server and we'll be more than happy to oblige! With that, I'll leave you with a bonus clip of a very important nighttime activity. Good night!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/U3NErDf.gif[/img]

notes.title: Meet The Sailor
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

We hope you're having a blast playing the prologue!

It's time to meet [b]The Sailor[/b]! The character that you will be playing as in Trading Time: A Croak Tale.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/b2bfc5b238c6161061a6372483fdabdab974a3ef.gif[/img]

While we'll still keep a lot of the narrative and background stuff under wraps at the moment (as the work is still in progress and subject to change), we'd like to showcase some of the visual aspects and early concept designs of our protagonist.

[h1]Early Concept Art[/h1]

Looking at some of our first concepts for the sailor, it's clear our lead artist, Casper, nailed down certain key elements of the character very early on.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/fa5717bbdca37a90a1c2efca17d45a7a6830259c.png[/img]

A couple of iterations later, softening the edges, tweaking the proportions, and losing the shoes, we ended up with the design we have today. It was important for us to convey the playfulness and tone of the game almost immediately with how the player character looked while still allowing for a range of expressiveness and personality when needed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/3e5a650c50525e90100d1aae6f0103d525c14484.png[/img]

Drawing a concept and designing a character is one thing but of course, we had to translate it to 3D, which is often a lot easier said than done! Luckily for us, Casper was also the one responsible for doing that, so really he only had himself to blame here!

[h1]2D Inspirations in 3D[/h1]

We took a lot of inspiration from traditional 2D animation, namely playing with scaling and proportions of moving parts commonly referred to as squash and stretch. Not only did this help sell the motion of our character but it also once again reinforced our toony visuals. 

Casper had to rig and skin the character quite unconventionally to allow for this but that's a more technical post for another time!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/2af3ce6009b97f2b41267523f321b7df176c327e.gif[/img]

If you scrub through these animations frame-by-frame you can see some very questionable single-frame poses as part of the character's animation. Definitely not realistic and somewhat nightmare-inducing but when you play it back at normal speed it's all of a sudden playful and bouncy - magic!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/285eece71962d40b1ae4fb38d8feef965bf08344.gif[/img]

We're also making use of both scaling and simple 2D sprites to animate The Sailor's mouth and eyes. This gives us a lot of control over the key elements of The Sailor's face, allowing us to be very expressive and convey a lot of personality to an otherwise simple character.

[h1]The Pipe[/h1]

As an additional bonus, one morning Casper came to the rest of the team and outlined specific pipe behavior that he claims came to him in a dream! Here at Half Past Yellow, we're all about achieving our pipe dreams so of course, we had to implement it! 

The gist of it is that the pipe looks most interesting as a silhouette in profile view instead of head-on in front of The Sailor's face or behind his head. As The Sailor moves around and rotates relative to the camera, the pipe tries its best to stay in profile as much as it can. 

It's very subtle and I'm sure it will be unnoticed by almost everyone, but now you know! It can be our shared little secret.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/bcfcf2eeafcdb807218c0c19ab65d5fda85f1d3b.gif[/img]

[h1]Moving On[/h1]

Designing a solid character visual that reacts and also controls well is truly a gift that keeps on giving and we're very happy to have put the effort in quite early in our development. Not only is it immensely satisfying to move around the world, but it is also very appealing to watch as The Sailor fluidly and without hesitation spreads mischief and creates clutter wherever they roam. 

On the other hand, we have definitely lost some (significant?) productivity aimlessly jumping around so the jury is still out on whether this has been the right move for us production-wise!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/4dd4cf10e1ff6865ebc40436e733af0cfeb148ad.gif[/img]

In any case, we're very excited and can't wait for you all to experience it for yourselves! Stay tuned for more previews and sneak peeks, and don't forget to follow us on our socials below if you haven't already!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1717510/Trading_Time_A_Croak_Tale/

notes.title: Welcome to the Trading Time: A Croak Tale Prologue
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41493886/7b0022bfe263006a6cb4ee13d39626d0400dd06e.png[/img]

Welcome to the Trading Time: A Croak Tale Prologue, a small, self-contained, mini-adventure. Join the sailor as he endeavours to unravel the mysteries of a barren island and the wizened old shaman who lives there.

Originally available as a demo at the Steam Nextfest, the prologue has now been updated to include a hatful of achievements. Play through the prologue’s story and escape the island but don’t forget all the extra tasks that will make those achievements pop!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41493886/d1123d5a0817e93459272651abc1caecee0a62fc.png[/img]

We hope you enjoy the Trading Time: A Croak Tale Prologue. Please be sure you let us know your thoughts.  If you really like the game, why not head over to the Trading Time: A Croak Tale Steam page and add it to your tour wishlist?
